components.note: A person shape in the middle.
Two smaller marks pressing in from either side, like being sandwiched.
十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'

example.hanzi: 他穿着一件黑色的夹克出门了。
example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe yī jiàn hēisè de jiākè chūmén le.
example.english: He went out wearing a black jacket.
example.fact: The zipper, patented in 1913 by Gideon Sundback, wasn't widely used in jackets until the 1920s when tailors adopted it for work clothes and, later, for the leather flight jackets worn by World War I aviators — before that, clothing relied mainly on buttons and hooks.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 违 involves stepping away from what is required, i.e. disobeying.
韦 (wéi) is an exact match for the sound of 违.
氵 (water/stream) — water naturally follows a fixed course, an image linked to the idea of 'law' or 'method.'
去 (to go/a course) — the path a stream follows suggested a regulated, consistent way of doing things, hence 'law, method.'

example.hanzi: 在这个国家赌博是违法的。
example.pinyin: Zài zhège guójiā dǔbó shì wéifǎ de.
example.english: Gambling is illegal in this country.
example.fact: The Code of Hammurabi, carved into a nearly eight-foot basalt stele around 1754 BC, is one of the earliest written legal codes still largely intact — its 282 laws covered everything from theft to divorce and famously prescribed 'an eye for an eye' punishments.

components.note: 邦 (a nation/state) — a community bound together
巾 (a flag/cloth) — a banner people rally around to support one another
氵 (water) — 派 relates to the flow and division of water.
The right side depicts a stream splitting into branching tributaries, giving 派 its extended meaning 'branch, faction, sect.'

example.hanzi: 那个城市里有好几个帮派互相争夺地盘。
example.pinyin: Nàge chéngshì lǐ yǒu hǎo jǐ gè bāngpài hùxiāng zhēngduó dìpán.
example.english: There are several gangs in that city fighting over turf.
example.fact: Sicily's Cosa Nostra traces its roots to 19th-century rural militias hired to protect landowners' estates; historians often point to the island's fragmented, feudal countryside as fertile ground for the loosely federated, family-based criminal organizations that emerged from it.

components.note: 阝 (mound/place) suggests a hidden spot behind a hill.
急 (worried, urgent) suggests someone anxiously ducking out of sight, giving 隐 its meaning 'to hide, conceal.'
禾 (grain) — grain was one of the first things ancient people owned and kept for themselves.
厶 pictures something folded in on itself and hidden away, giving 私 its sense of 'private, personal, one's own.'

example.hanzi: 很多人担心社交媒体会侵犯他们的隐私。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō rén dānxīn shèjiāo méitǐ huì qīnfàn tāmen de yǐnsī.
example.english: Many people worry that social media will invade their privacy.
example.fact: The right to privacy as a distinct legal concept was first articulated in an 1890 Harvard Law Review article by Samuel Warren and Louis Brandeis, written partly in response to intrusive newspaper coverage of Warren's own family — it later shaped landmark U.S. Supreme Court privacy rulings.

components.note: 行 (to go/walk) — 街 names a road where people walk and travel.
圭 (guī) gives a sound distantly related to jiē, having drifted apart over time.
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

example.hanzi: 周末街头挤满了逛街的人。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò jiētóu jǐmǎn le guàngjiē de rén.
example.english: On the weekend the streets were packed with shoppers.
example.fact: Pompeii's streets, preserved under volcanic ash since 79 AD, still show worn ruts from cart wheels and raised stepping stones that let pedestrians cross without stepping in flooded gutters — an ancient solution to the same street-drainage problem modern cities still wrestle with.

components.note: 冂 (an enclosure or doorway) — 内 pictures the space one enters.
人 (person) — a person entering an enclosure gave 内 its meaning 'inside' or 'within.'
A drawing of a robe's collar and folded sides, seen from the front.

example.hanzi: 她在行李箱里放了几件内衣。
example.pinyin: Tā zài xínglixiāng lǐ fàng le jǐ jiàn nèiyī.
example.english: She packed a few pieces of underwear in her suitcase.
example.fact: Archaeologists found a roughly 600-year-old linen bra among artifacts in an Austrian castle in 2008, pushing back the known history of supportive women's undergarments by centuries — before the find, bras were generally thought to be a 19th-century invention.

components.note: Ancient forms show a person wearing an elaborate mask or headdress, thought to depict a ceremonial dancer performing summer rain-and-harvest rituals — the origin of 夏's meaning 'summer' and, by extension, the name of China's first dynasty.
戌 (a halberd/weapon) — represents armed force.
女 (woman) — force used to intimidate gave 威 its meaning 'power, might, awe-inspiring.'
大 depicts a person, seen from the front with arms and legs spread.
弓 (a bow) shows the person carrying a weapon — together an early image of an armed outsider.

example.hanzi: 我们计划明年夏天去夏威夷旅行。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen jìhuà míngnián xiàtiān qù Xiàwēiyí lǚxíng.
example.english: We're planning to travel to Hawaii next summer.
example.fact: The Hawaiian Islands formed one by one as the Pacific tectonic plate slid slowly over a stationary hotspot of rising magma; because the plate keeps moving northwest, the islands get progressively older in that direction, with the still-erupting Big Island the youngest of the chain.

components.note: 力 (strength/effort) — the exertion behind the achievement.
工 (work/labor) — results produced through skillful labor, giving 功 its meaning 'achievement, merit, skill.'
Originally a drawing of a bear, with 厶 as its head, ⺼ as its body, and 匕匕 as its claws; the picture was later borrowed to mean 'ability, to be able to.'

example.hanzi: 这款手机有很多实用的功能。
example.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn shǒujī yǒu hěn duō shíyòng de gōngnéng.
example.english: This phone has many practical functions.
example.fact: The human appendix, long dismissed as a useless evolutionary leftover, is now believed by many biologists to serve as a safe house for beneficial gut bacteria, letting the digestive system quickly recolonize itself with healthy microbes after a severe bout of illness like diarrhea.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — ancient texts were written on bound bamboo strips, and 第 originally referred to the sequential order of such strips, giving rise to its meaning 'ordinal number' (as in 第一, first).
A simple cross-shaped mark, likely originally a cut or notch used for tallying — the shape was assigned to represent the number seven early in the script's history.

example.hanzi: 这是他第七次参加马拉松比赛。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì tā dì qī cì cānjiā mǎlāsōng bǐsài.
example.english: This is the seventh time he has taken part in a marathon.
example.fact: Saturn is the seventh planet counting outward from the Sun, but it was the last of the seven 'classical planets' visible to the naked eye — the ones ancient astronomers could track across the sky without any telescope.

components.note: 日 (sun) — combined with 月 (moon), 明 shows the light of both sun and moon, giving the meaning 'bright' or 'clear.'
月 (moon) — together with 日 (sun), the two brightest things in the sky represent brightness and clarity.
石 (stone) — 确 originally meant firm and solid like stone, extending to 'true, accurate, indeed.'
角 (jiǎo) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from què.

example.hanzi: 老师明确地解释了考试的规则。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī míngquè de jiěshì le kǎoshì de guīzé.
example.english: The teacher clearly explained the rules for the exam.
example.fact: The Plain Writing Act, signed into U.S. law in 2010, requires federal agencies to write public documents in clear, direct language — follow-up studies found that plainly written government forms cut citizen error rates and call-center volume by as much as half.

components.note: 口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.
立 here depicts a tongue positioned to speak.
日 here depicts an open mouth — a tongue forming sound in the mouth gave 音 its meaning 'sound, tone.'

example.hanzi: 他说英语带有很重的法国口音。
example.pinyin: Tā shuō Yīngyǔ dài yǒu hěn zhòng de Fǎguó kǒuyīn.
example.english: He speaks English with a heavy French accent.
example.fact: Foreign accent syndrome is a rare neurological condition, usually triggered by a stroke or brain injury, in which patients suddenly begin speaking their own native language with what sounds like a foreign accent — fewer than 100 cases have been documented worldwide since it was first described in 1907.

components.note: 门 (gate, door) marks a boundary being crossed.
马 (horse) rushes through the gate — a horse charging in, giving 闯 its meaning 'to rush in, to dash.'
入 depicts a simple wedge or arrow shape pointing inward, showing the direction of entering.

example.hanzi: 一只野猫闯入了我们的花园。
example.pinyin: Yī zhī yěmāo chuǎngrù le wǒmen de huāyuán.
example.english: A wild cat broke into our garden.
example.fact: In 2020, wild boars increasingly wandered into Barcelona's streets and parks as pandemic lockdowns emptied cities of people — a pattern seen in other quiet urban areas too, showing how quickly wildlife adapts to sudden drops in human activity.

components.note: 方 here depicts a banner or flag flying from a pole, marking where troops are gathered.
疋 depicts a pair of marching feet — moving beneath the flag 方, the image gave 旋 its meaning 'to circle around, to return.'
车 (cart) — relates to 转's meaning 'to turn, change direction,' like a wheel turning.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 转 is pronounced zhuǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 摩天轮缓缓地旋转着。
example.pinyin: Mótiānlún huǎnhuǎn de xuánzhuǎn zhe.
example.english: The Ferris wheel slowly rotated.
example.fact: Venus rotates so slowly, and in the opposite direction from most planets, that a single day there — one full rotation — takes about 243 Earth days, longer than the roughly 225 Earth days it takes Venus to complete an orbit around the Sun.

components.note: 口 (mouth), stacked three times — many mouths talking about or judging something, the source of 品's meaning 'product, item; quality, rank.'
片 (a thin slice/board) — 牌 names a flat board or sign, like a nameplate.
卑 (bēi) gives a sound close to pái.

example.hanzi: 这个品牌以质量好而出名。
example.pinyin: Zhège pǐnpái yǐ zhìliàng hǎo ér chūmíng.
example.english: This brand is known for its high quality.
example.fact: The Bass Red Triangle, used by the British brewer Bass since the 1870s, became the United Kingdom's first registered trademark in 1876 when a new trademark law took effect — legend holds that a company clerk camped outside the registry office overnight to be first in line.

components.note: 牙 (tooth) — teeth piercing or boring through something, the origin of 'to pierce'
穴 (xué) gives a sound distantly related to 穿's reading chuān, having drifted apart considerably over time
走 (run/walk) — relates to 越's meaning 'to exceed, cross over,' running past a boundary.
戉 (yuè) gives the sound — 越 is also pronounced yuè, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 这条隧道穿越了整座山。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo suìdào chuānyuè le zhěng zuò shān.
example.english: This tunnel goes through the entire mountain.
example.fact: The Gotthard Base Tunnel in the Swiss Alps, opened in 2016, runs for about 35 miles beneath the mountains and took 17 years to bore — engineers had to cool the rock face, which reached temperatures above 45°C (113°F) from geothermal heat deep underground.

components.note: 月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.
心 (heart/mind) — 意 relates to thought, intention, and meaning, things of the mind.
音 (yīn) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading has drifted from yì, though both share a similar vowel.

example.hanzi: 他有意避开了这个话题。
example.pinyin: Tā yǒuyì bìkāi le zhège huàtí.
example.english: He intentionally avoided this topic.
example.fact: Studies in cognitive psychology find that people consistently judge accidental harms less severely than intentional ones with identical outcomes — a pattern researchers call the 'intentionality bias,' which shows up even in young children's moral judgments by around age four.

components.note: 回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'
页 (head) — 顾 originally related to turning the head to look back at something
厄 (è) gives a sound distantly related to 顾's reading gù, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 年终的时候公司会回顾这一年的业绩。
example.pinyin: Niánzhōng de shíhou gōngsī huì huígù zhè yī nián de yèjì.
example.english: At year's end, the company reviews its performance for the year.
example.fact: At Carl Sagan's request, Voyager 1 turned its camera around in 1990 to take one last look back at Earth from about 3.7 billion miles away — the resulting 'Pale Blue Dot' photograph shows the planet as a single pixel of light against the vastness of space.

components.note: 子 (child) forms the left side of the character.
小, standing in for a connecting thread in the traditional form 孫, links generations together, giving 孙 its meaning 'grandchild, descendant.'
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 爷爷最喜欢带着孙子去公园。
example.pinyin: Yéye zuì xǐhuan dàizhe sūnzi qù gōngyuán.
example.english: Grandpa likes taking his grandson to the park most of all.
example.fact: The 'grandmother hypothesis' in evolutionary biology proposes that human females evolved unusually long post-reproductive lifespans specifically because grandmothers who helped raise grandchildren improved those children's survival odds — a pattern rarely seen in other mammals.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 把 relates to grasping or holding something with the hand.
巴 (bā) gives the sound — 把 is pronounced bǎ, a close match differing only in tone.
扌 (hand) — 握 describes an action done with the hand: grasping tightly.
屋 (wū) gives a sound distantly related to wò, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 我们要把握住这个难得的机会。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yào bǎwò zhù zhège nándé de jīhuì.
example.english: We must seize this rare opportunity.
example.fact: Peregrine falcons seize their prey mid-air by folding their wings and diving at speeds exceeding 240 mph, making them the fastest animals on Earth — the strike, called a 'stoop,' can generate enough force to kill a pigeon instantly.

components.note: Woman — an old semantic root sometimes linked to feelings.
Gives the sound jiān, related to xián but drifted apart over time.
疋 — a person walking, shown pausing and looking back uncertainly
矢 (an arrow/cane) — an old man's walking stick, held while hesitating
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 警方逮捕了一名抢劫案的嫌疑人。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng dàibǔ le yī míng qiǎngjié àn de xiányírén.
example.english: Police arrested a suspect in the robbery case.
example.fact: Fingerprint identification became a standard tool for identifying criminal suspects after Argentine police officer Juan Vucetich used it in 1892 to solve a murder case, matching a bloody thumbprint at the scene to the victim's mother — one of the first murder convictions based on fingerprint evidence.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 激 originally described water dashing or surging forcefully
敫 (jiǎo) gives a sound distantly related to 激's reading jī, having drifted apart over time
灬 (fire) — 烈 relates to something as intense and fierce as fire
列 (liè) gives the sound — an exact match with 烈's reading liè

example.hanzi: 两队之间的比赛非常激烈。
example.pinyin: Liǎng duì zhījiān de bǐsài fēicháng jīliè.
example.english: The match between the two teams was extremely intense.
example.fact: Male elephant seals fight fierce, sometimes bloody battles for beachmaster status during breeding season, rearing up to slam their chests together — the winner may father the vast majority of pups on a beach, while most other males father none at all.

components.note: 玉 (jade, shown without its dot) represents something valuable.
厶 beneath suggests something slipping away privately, giving 丢 its meaning 'to lose, to throw away.'
扌 (hand) — 掉 relates to dropping something from the hand.
卓 (zhuó) reflects an older phonetic connection that has faded in the modern pronunciation diào.

example.hanzi: 他不小心把钱包丢掉了。
example.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn bǎ qiánbāo diūdiào le.
example.english: He accidentally lost his wallet.
example.fact: Rubber ducks and sneakers from a 1990 cargo spill in the Pacific became unlikely tools for oceanographers studying ocean currents — tracking where the thousands of lost shoes washed ashore over the following years helped refine models of the North Pacific gyre's circulation.

meanings: camera (abbr. for 照相機|照相机[zhao4 xiang4 ji1])

components.note: 木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'
木 (wood) — 机 originally referred to a wooden device or machine, such as a loom.
几 depicts a small table or stool — combined with 木 (wood), the character pictured a wooden machine or mechanism.

example.hanzi: 她用相机拍下了日落的美景。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng xiàngjī pāixià le rìluò de měijǐng.
example.english: She used her camera to capture the beautiful sunset.
example.fact: The first permanent photograph, taken around 1826 or 1827 by Nicéphore Niépce, required an exposure time of about eight hours pointed out a window — the hazy resulting image of rooftops and a barn is the oldest surviving camera photograph.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 授 means to give or hand something over.
受 (shòu) gives the sound — an exact match with 授.
木 (wood) — 权 originally meant a wooden lever or weight, later extended to 'power, authority, right.'
雚 was historically closer to guàn; the pronunciation has since shifted to quán, so the sound link is faint today.

example.hanzi: 公司授权他代表签署合同。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī shòuquán tā dàibiǎo qiānshǔ hétong.
example.english: The company authorized him to sign the contract on its behalf.
example.fact: Modern computer security borrows a distinction formalized in 1970s access-control research, which separated 'authentication' (proving who you are) from 'authorization' (determining what you're allowed to do) — a split still fundamental to how banks and governments secure digital systems today.

components.note: 豕 (pig/boar) — appears as part of 象's original full-body pictograph of an elephant, reusing a four-legged-animal shape; 象 itself depicts an elephant's trunk and ears above the body.
Traditionally analyzed as 日 combined with 疋, linked to the idea of speaking directly and truthfully — the source of 是's meaning 'to be, indeed, right.'

example.hanzi: 这朵云看起来象是一只兔子。
example.pinyin: Zhè duǒ yún kànqǐlái xiàng shì yī zhī tùzi.
example.english: This cloud looks as if it's a rabbit.
example.fact: The tendency to see meaningful shapes, like faces or animals, in random patterns such as clouds is called pareidolia — it's thought to be a byproduct of a brain wired to spot faces quickly, since rapidly recognizing a face offered our ancestors a survival advantage.

components.note: 又 stands in for the original, more complex phonetic element 雚 (a heron) used in the traditional form 歡; the simplification kept the shape without borrowing its meaning.
欠 (an open mouth, as in yawning or exhaling) — a wide-open mouth suggested laughing or shouting for joy, giving 欢 its meaning 'happy, joyful.'
乐 is the simplified form of 樂, which depicted a wooden 木 instrument strung with strings 幺, played with a pick 白 — music came to represent joy, giving 乐 its meaning 'happy, music.'

example.hanzi: 孩子们的笑声充满了欢乐。
example.pinyin: Háizimen de xiàoshēng chōngmǎn le huānlè.
example.english: The children's laughter was full of joy.
example.fact: A 2005 University of Maryland study found that laughter measurably relaxes blood vessels: watching a stressful film narrowed participants' blood vessels, while watching a comedy widened them, an effect on blood flow the researchers compared to light exercise.

components.note: 龶 depicts a poisonous plant, tying 毒 to its meaning 'poison.'
母 (mǔ) gives a rhyme close to dú, with the initial shifted.
贝 (money) — 贩 relates to trading for profit.
反 (fǎn) gives a sound close to fàn, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 警方成功抓获了一名毒贩。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng chénggōng zhuōhuò le yī míng dúfàn.
example.english: Police successfully caught a drug dealer.
example.fact: Opium smuggling into China by British traders in the 19th century grew so large-scale that it triggered the First Opium War (1839–1842); the conflict ended with China ceding Hong Kong to Britain, one of history's starkest examples of a drug trade reshaping geopolitics.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — grain stalks bending and swaying in the wind.
女 (woman) — a woman bending pliantly, an image of yielding compliance that gave 委 its meanings 'to entrust, to appoint' and 'listless, indirect.'
扌 (hand) — a hand held out, palm up
乇 — something resting on the upturned palm for support
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 律师向委托人解释了案件的进展。
example.pinyin: Lǜshī xiàng wěituōrén jiěshì le ànjiàn de jìnzhǎn.
example.english: The lawyer explained the progress of the case to the client.
example.fact: The legal concept of a trust, where one party manages assets for a client's benefit, traces back to medieval English 'uses' devised by knights heading off on the Crusades, who transferred land to a trusted friend to manage while they were away — an arrangement that evolved into modern trust law.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with an implement) — relates to 收's meaning 'to receive, collect, harvest.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shōu.
入 depicts a simple wedge or arrow shape pointing inward, showing the direction of entering.

example.hanzi: 他的月收入比去年增加了不少。
example.pinyin: Tā de yuè shōurù bǐ qùnián zēngjiā le bù shǎo.
example.english: His monthly income has increased quite a bit compared to last year.
example.fact: The Gini coefficient, a number between 0 and 1 used to measure income inequality within a country, was developed by Italian statistician Corrado Gini in 1912 — a score of 0 represents perfect equality, while 1 represents a hypothetical situation where a single person holds all the income.

components.note: 耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.
Ancient forms show a stake wound with cord in a spiraling, ordered pattern — a symbol of sequence and rank among siblings that gave 弟 its meaning 'younger brother.'

example.hanzi: 老弟，好久不见，最近怎么样？
example.pinyin: Lǎodì, hǎojiǔ bú jiàn, zuìjìn zěnmeyàng?
example.english: Old pal, long time no see, how have you been lately?
example.fact: A famous 75-year Harvard study following the same group of men from young adulthood into old age found that close, warm relationships were the single strongest predictor of health and happiness in later life — stronger than wealth, fame, or even cholesterol levels.

meanings: (Tw) to repeatedly nod one's head while dozing

components.note: 钅 (metal) shows the material of the fishing hook.
勺 depicts a small curved shape, echoed in the curve of a fishing hook.
鱼 is a simplified picture of a fish — the top traces its head and fins, and the strokes below represent its body and tail.

example.hanzi: 周末爸爸经常带我去河边钓鱼。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò bàba jīngcháng dài wǒ qù hébiān diàoyú.
example.english: On weekends, Dad often takes me fishing by the river.
example.fact: Archaeologists have found fish hooks made from shell dating back roughly 23,000 years at a cave site on Okinawa, among the oldest known fishing tools in the world — evidence that early humans there were already skilled anglers well before the last Ice Age ended.

components.note: 八 here depicts something splitting apart or being divided.
厶 is an old form meaning 'private' or 'one's own' — 公 shows dividing up private property to share it fairly, giving rise to the meaning 'public' or 'fair.'
田 (farmland) over 土 (earth/soil) — originally referred to a village or a measured unit of farmland, later extended to mean 'inside' or a unit of distance.

example.hanzi: 从这里到市中心大约十公里。
example.pinyin: Cóng zhèlǐ dào shì zhōngxīn dàyuē shí gōnglǐ.
example.english: It's about ten kilometers from here to downtown.
example.fact: The meter was originally defined in 1793 by French scientists as one ten-millionth of the distance from the North Pole to the equator along a line through Paris — a definition later found to be slightly inaccurate, since the meter is now defined instead using the speed of light.

components.note: 隹 (a bird) — one of a flock.
木 (a tree) — birds flocking together on a tree, the image of gathering that gave 集 its meaning 'to gather, collect; a collection.'
Depicts a lid fitting closed over a container or mouth (口) below — the image of two parts fitting perfectly together gave 合 its meaning 'to combine, to close, to fit.'

example.hanzi: 全班同学在操场上集合。
example.pinyin: Quán bān tóngxué zài cāochǎng shàng jíhé.
example.english: The whole class gathered on the sports field.
example.fact: Set theory, the mathematical study of collections of objects, was largely founded single-handedly by Georg Cantor in the 1870s — his radical claim that some infinities are larger than others provoked fierce resistance from contemporaries but now underlies nearly all of modern mathematics.

components.note: A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'
立 (to stand) — 站 relates to standing, and by extension a stop or station where one stands to wait
占 (zhàn) gives the sound — 站 is also pronounced zhàn, an exact match

example.hanzi: 我们在车站等了半个小时的火车。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài chēzhàn děng le bàn gè xiǎoshí de huǒchē.
example.english: We waited half an hour for the train at the station.
example.fact: Grand Central Terminal in New York City has a ceiling mural of the night sky painted backwards; the more likely explanation, despite a popular legend blaming a copying error, is that it was meant to be viewed as if from beyond the stars, looking down at Earth.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — grain was one of the first things ancient people owned and kept for themselves.
厶 pictures something folded in on itself and hidden away, giving 私 its sense of 'private, personal, one's own.'
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.

example.hanzi: 他私下告诉我这个秘密。
example.pinyin: Tā sīxià gàosu wǒ zhège mìmì.
example.english: He told me this secret in private.
example.fact: Confidential employee counseling services, an early form of private workplace consultation, began appearing in some U.S. companies in the 1970s as employers experimented with what became known as employee assistance programs — a forerunner of today's confidential HR hotlines.

components.note: 扌 (hand) shows 抚 relates to a gentle action done by hand.
无 (wú) gives a sound distantly related to fǔ, having drifted apart over time.
儿 (child) — 养 relates to raising and nurturing children or animals
羊 (yáng) gives a sound close to 养's reading yǎng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 她独自抚养两个孩子长大。
example.pinyin: Tā dúzì fǔyǎng liǎng gè háizi zhǎngdà.
example.english: She raised two children by herself.
example.fact: Emperor penguin fathers incubate a single egg alone for about two months through the brutal Antarctic winter, balancing it on their feet and huddling with other males in temperatures that can drop below -60°C, while the mothers travel far out to sea to feed.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — an older sense of 秘 was linked to grain kept out of sight, before it narrowed to 'secret.'
必 (bì) gives the sound — an exact match with 秘.
⺺ — an abstract mark meant to depict strokes made by a writing brush, the origin of 书's meaning 'book, document, letter.'

example.hanzi: 秘书正在安排经理明天的会议。
example.pinyin: Mìshū zhèngzài ānpái jīnglǐ míngtiān de huìyì.
example.english: The secretary is arranging the manager's meeting for tomorrow.
example.fact: In ancient Rome, secretarial-type work was often performed by educated enslaved people or freedmen called amanuenses, who took dictation and managed correspondence for wealthy patrons — the statesman Cicero relied heavily on his secretary Tiro, credited with inventing an early shorthand system.

meanings: (zoology) segment (of the body of a worm, centipede etc)

components.note: 王 (a variant of 玉, jade) — 环 originally referred to a round jade ring or bracelet
不 (bù) gives a sound distantly related to 环's reading huán, having drifted apart considerably over time
节 is the simplified form of 節, which depicted the segmented sections of a bamboo stalk ⺮ — giving 节 its meaning 'joint, section, festival.'

example.hanzi: 这个项目的每个环节都很重要。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiàngmù de měi gè huánjié dōu hěn zhòngyào.
example.english: Every link in this project is important.
example.fact: Earthworms have segmented bodies made up of more than a hundred ring-like sections, each with its own set of muscles and nerve tissue — this segmentation lets the worm contract and extend sections independently, which is exactly how it powers its way through soil.

components.note: 凡 (common/ordinary) — suggests something shared or held in common.
口 (mouth) — sharing a common mouth/voice with others gave 同 its meaning of 'same, together.'
亻 (person) — 伴 describes a person accompanying another.
半 (bàn) is an exact match for the sound of 伴.

example.hanzi: 登山的时候一定要有同伴。
example.pinyin: Dēngshān de shíhou yídìng yào yǒu tóngbàn.
example.english: When climbing mountains, you must have a companion.
example.fact: Several tamarin and marmoset species practice cooperative breeding, where non-parent group members help carry and feed infants — a rare arrangement outside humans that researchers link to the evolution of unusually complex social bonds among primates.

components.note: Depicts two things splayed apart from each other — such as a bird's two wings, or two people standing back-to-back — later used for the meaning 'not, contrary to.'
寸 (a hand) reaching for 旦 (originally 貝, a shell used as currency) — a picture of grasping something valuable, hence 'to obtain, to get.'

example.hanzi: 你非得现在就走吗？
example.pinyin: Nǐ fēiděi xiànzài jiù zǒu ma?
example.english: Do you absolutely have to leave right now?
example.fact: The three-point seatbelt, invented in 1959 by Volvo engineer Nils Bohlin, wasn't required by law in most of the United States until the 1980s — Volvo made the patent freely available to every other car manufacturer, a decision credited with saving an estimated million lives worldwide.

components.note: 入 (enter, put away) — 全 pictures something being placed into safekeeping.
玉 (jade) — a valuable treasure kept whole and undamaged, giving 全 its meaning of 'complete' or 'entire.'
亻 (person) — 体 relates to the human body.
本 (root, basis) — the body as the fundamental basis of a person, giving 体 its meaning 'body, form, style.'

example.hanzi: 全体员工都参加了年会。
example.pinyin: Quántǐ yuángōng dōu cānjiā le niánhuì.
example.english: All the staff attended the annual meeting.
example.fact: Starling flocks called murmurations can involve tens of thousands of birds moving as a single fluid shape, changing direction within milliseconds — physicists studying the phenomenon found each bird reacts mainly to its seven nearest neighbors, a simple rule that produces the flock's dazzling coordinated motion.

components.note: Ancient forms depict a hand grasping a forked instrument or tally used by officials recording government affairs — the origin of 事's meaning 'matter, affair, to serve.'
止 (a foot, stepping forward) — 先 pictures someone moving ahead of another.
儿 (a person) — one person stepping ahead of another gave 先 its meaning 'before' or 'first.'

example.hanzi: 请事先通知我们你的到达时间。
example.pinyin: Qǐng shìxiān tōngzhī wǒmen nǐ de dàodá shíjiān.
example.english: Please notify us of your arrival time in advance.
example.fact: Japan's earthquake early warning system can give residents several seconds to tens of seconds of advance notice before shaking arrives, by detecting a quake's faster-traveling P-waves and racing an alert ahead of the slower, more destructive S-waves — often just enough time to stop a train or step away from a shelf.

meanings: to be the one in charge

components.note: 讠 (speech radical) — shows 说 relates to talking or language
兑 (duì) is the phonetic component; historically 说 was also pronounced closer to 兑's sound before shifting to shuō
Depicts a child wrapped in swaddling, related to 子 (child); the picture-meaning has nothing to do with its modern grammatical role marking a completed action or change of state.
⺮ (bamboo) — the material of ancient counting rods.
具 (held in two hands) — bamboo counting rods or an abacus held up for use, the tools of calculation that gave 算 its meaning 'to calculate, count.'

example.hanzi: 在这个家里，一切都是爸爸说了算。
example.pinyin: Zài zhège jiā lǐ, yīqiè dōu shì bàba shuōlesuàn.
example.english: In this family, everything is decided by Dad — he has the final say.
example.fact: In many wild wolf packs, one breeding pair makes most decisions about when the pack hunts, moves, or rests; researchers who've tracked packs for decades find the pair usually earns that role through age and parentage rather than constant fighting, contradicting the popular myth of violent dominance battles.

components.note: Simplified from 凱, which combined 豈 (used here mainly for its sound) with 几 — together forming a character used for 'triumphant, victorious,' as in the phrase 凱旋 (kǎixuán), 'to return in triumph.'
艹 (plant) — 蒂 names the stem that attaches a fruit or flower to its plant.
帝 (dì) gives the sound — an exact match with 蒂.

example.hanzi: 凯蒂是我们班最会画画的学生。
example.pinyin: Kǎidì shì wǒmen bān zuì huì huàhuà de xuésheng.
example.english: Katy is the best painter in our class.
example.fact: Hello Kitty, whose full name is Kitty White, was designed in 1974 by Yuko Shimizu for the Japanese company Sanrio — despite widespread assumptions, the character has always officially been a fictional British schoolgirl, not a cat, according to Sanrio's own backstory for her.

components.note: Simplified from 盡, which pictured a hand with a brush cleaning the last remains out of a dish (皿) — the image of using something down to the very end gave 尽 its meaning 'to exhaust, to the utmost, entirely.'
忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 大家在派对上尽情跳舞。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā zài pàiduì shàng jìnqíng tiàowǔ.
example.english: Everyone danced to their heart's content at the party.
example.fact: Bees perform what's called a 'waggle dance' to tell hive mates the direction and distance of a food source — discovered by Karl von Frisch in the 1940s, the dance's angle relative to the sun encodes the direction, work that later won him a Nobel Prize.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 啦 is a sentence-final particle, spoken from the mouth.
拉 (lā) is an exact match for the sound of 啦.
口 (mouth) — 啦 is a sentence-final particle, spoken from the mouth.
拉 (lā) is an exact match for the sound of 啦.
阝 (a mound or place) — 队 pictures people gathering together.
人 (person) — people gathering in one place gave 队 its meaning 'a team' or 'a line/queue.'

example.hanzi: 啦啦队在场边为运动员加油。
example.pinyin: Lālāduì zài chǎngbiān wèi yùndòngyuán jiāyóu.
example.english: The cheerleading squad cheered for the athletes from the sidelines.
example.fact: Organized cheerleading began in the United States in 1898 when University of Minnesota student Johnny Campbell led a crowd in a coordinated cheer during a football game — for decades the activity was overwhelmingly male, and women didn't dominate cheerleading squads until World War II sent many college men off to fight.

meanings: this (classifier used before films, books, or other works)

components.note: 辶 (to walk, to move) — 这 originally related to movement or approach, before narrowing to the demonstrative 'this.'
文 replaces the original phonetic element 言 used in the traditional form 這, chosen for its simpler shape rather than for sound or meaning.
阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).

example.hanzi: 这部电影讲述了一个感人的故事。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎngshù le yī gè gǎnrén de gùshi.
example.english: This film tells a moving story.
example.fact: The Lumière brothers' 1896 film 'Arrival of a Train at La Ciotat' is famously, though probably apocryphally, said to have caused audience members to flee their seats in fear of being run over by the oncoming train — one of cinema's earliest urban legends about the power of the moving image.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 做 relates to a person carrying out an action.
故 (cause, reason, to happen) — combined with 亻 (person), 做 came to mean 'to make' or 'to do,' someone actively causing something to happen.
饣 (food) — 饭 names cooked rice, a meal.
反 (fǎn) gives the sound — an exact match with 饭.

example.hanzi: 妈妈每天晚上都会做饭。
example.pinyin: Māma měitiān wǎnshang dōu huì zuòfàn.
example.english: Mom cooks dinner every evening.
example.fact: Primatologist Richard Wrangham's 'cooking hypothesis' argues that the invention of cooking, roughly 1.8 million years ago, was a turning point in human evolution — cooked food is easier to digest and yields more usable calories, energy that may have helped fuel the growth of larger human brains.

components.note: 忄 (heart, mind) — 怪 relates to a feeling: surprise or unease at something unusual.
圣 here serves only as a sound element, unrelated to its separate meaning 'sage'; it gives a sound distantly related to guài, having drifted apart over time.
丷 (horns) at the top shows the animal's horns.
田 (here shaped like a head with eyes) in the middle represents the animal's face.
口 (mouth) at the bottom completes the creature's face, giving 兽 its meaning 'beast, animal.'

example.hanzi: 电影里的怪兽摧毁了整座城市。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de guàishòu cuīhuǐ le zhěng zuò chéngshì.
example.english: The monster in the movie destroyed the entire city.
example.fact: Godzilla, one of cinema's most famous monsters, was created in 1954 partly as a metaphor for the destructive power of nuclear weapons, following Japan's experience with the atomic bombings and hydrogen bomb testing in the Pacific — its design drew on both a Tyrannosaurus and an iguana.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 基 relates to the ground or foundation something is built on.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 基 is pronounced jī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
石 (stone) — 础 names the stone base of a pillar or building.
出 (chū) gives a sound distantly related to chǔ, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 良好的教育是成功的基础。
example.pinyin: Liánghǎo de jiàoyù shì chénggōng de jīchǔ.
example.english: A good education is the foundation of success.
example.fact: The Leaning Tower of Pisa began tilting almost as soon as construction started in 1173, because its foundation was laid on soft, unstable soil only about 10 feet deep — engineers didn't fully stabilize the tower until a major restoration project completed in 2001 straightened it by roughly 1.5 degrees.
